messages:
Eli: rolling docRanker-v1.1-ptq to staging for a quick quality pass. weird signal: NDCG up slightly but MRR tank on queries that include inline code/HTML. posting numbers.

EvalBot: offline compare docRanker-v1.1-ptq -> baseline fp32
EvalBot: NDCG@10: 0.813 -> 0.817 (+0.004)
EvalBot: MRR@10: 0.645 -> 0.602 (-0.043)  <-- >75% of MRR loss from queries containing markup or backticked code

Maya: that's a big top-1 hit concentrated on a syntactic slice. examples?

Eli: samples: "how to parse <code>\u003cdiv>\u003c/span>" -> baseline top1 was page A, ptq now favors page B
Eli: "best regex for `\w+@\w+\.com`" -> ranking flips
Eli: "api: POST /v1/items - sample body \n {\"name\": \"x\"}" shows literal braces tokenized oddly

Rohit: likely cause: training/labeling pipeline stripped HTML and unescaped code; eval still has raw HTML/backticks. tokenizer and the model see different token streams causing short-sequence sensitivity in PTQ.

Tessa: small QA note: our UI masks < and > in logs which made these look like plain text earlier. we should add raw_hex and raw_escaped fields to eval export.

Maya: two quick triage runs:
Maya: 1) re-run eval with HTML-stripped + unescape = true (mirror training)
Maya: 2) re-run eval with explicit keep-markup to see if model learned to use markup tokens (sanity check)

Eli: re-eval (HTML-stripped/unescaped):
EvalBot: NDCG@10: 0.813 -> 0.815
EvalBot: MRR@10: 0.645 -> 0.631
EvalBot: (MRR gap reduced to -0.014)

Rohit: great, that explains most of it. residual ~0.014 could be PTQ kernel sensitivity or slight mismatch in snippet extraction between train & eval. next steps:
Rohit: - add raw_hex + markup_stripped + snippet_mode to eval CSV
Rohit: - run a 50k cleaned vs raw eval (compare slices: inline-code, html-tags, json-snippets)
Rohit: - ablate PTQ: try per-channel int8 and alternative clip-thresholds for 4-bit PTQ

Tessa: infra ask: please include candidate_snippet_renderer flag in CSV (how candidate text was produced: html_to_text | head_only | head_tail). we had a prod incident where serving used html_to_text but eval harness used head_only.

Maya: command to reproduce the cleaned eval locally:
Maya: ```bash
Maya: python infra/eval_harness.py \\
Maya:   --model docRanker-v1.1-ptq \\
Maya:   --dataset markup_holdout \\
Maya:   --normalize markup_strip_unescape \\
Maya:   --limit 20000 \\
Maya: ```

InfraBot: canary deploy: docRanker-v1.1-ptq -> canary (tag: canary-2026-06-10-docrankv1.1)

Eli: operational decision: if cleaned eval removes >0.02 MRR gap, we should standardize markup stripping in serving ingest to match training. otherwise, pick the PTQ kernel that reduces residual and add a regression monitor for markup slice.

Rohit: i'll kick off the 50k re-eval and the PTQ kernel ablation tomorrow morning. i'll upload CSVs gzipped to s3://redwood-evals/docranker/v1.1/ and include a .meta with normalization flags.

Tessa: QA will also do a manual review of representative pairs (raw vs stripped) to check whether the stripped text loses signal we should preserve. flagging this for product if stripping removes important UI cues.

Maya: tiny infra PR i'll open today: add raw_hex, markup_stripped, snippet_mode, and renderer_flag to eval output + a --normalize-markup boolean. keeps default off so we don't surprise other experiments.

Eli: thanks team. please tag me on the PR and drop the eval artifacts in #eng-ml when ready. we'll reconvene after the 50k run and decide serving vs kernel mitigation. :thumbsup:
